What Superior1 does

Superior1 Towing LLC offers four services: light duty towing, recovery, roadside assistance and equipment transportation. Below is what each one covers and what to tell us when you call. Look for the red trucks with the Superior1 name and chain stripe on the door.

Light duty towing

For a vehicle that broke down, won't start, or has to get to a shop, a yard or back home. A flatbed carries the whole vehicle off the ground, which helps when it won't roll straight or sits too low to be lifted by the wheels.

Cars and SUVs
Everyday towing for breakdowns and cars that won't start. Have the year, make and model ready, and tell us if the wheels turn and the steering works.
Low and lowered vehicles
Dropped trucks, lowered cars and anything with little ground clearance. Mention body kits, air suspension or a low front lip so we can plan before we load.
Trucks and lifted trucks
Pickups, lifted trucks and work trucks. Tell us the tire size if it's lifted, whether there's a rack or tool body, and whether the bed is loaded, because height and weight matter.
Trailers and boats
Trailer towing and boat towing. Tell us the length, whether it's empty or loaded, and if the tires, hitch and axles are in good shape.
Special vehicles
For vehicles that need extra planning, such as a motorhome. Send the length, height and a picture and we'll tell you if we can take it.
Call (209) 612-9092or text us about a tow

Motorcycle towing

Motorcycle towing is on our service list. The bike rides strapped down on the flatbed, off the ground, whether it broke down, won't start or went down on the road. The photo here is a real Superior1 job.

Breakdowns and no-starts
For a bike that quit on the road or won't fire up at home. Tell us the make and model, and whether it rolls in neutral.
After a crash or a drop
For a bike that went down or left the road. Tell us if anything is bent, leaking or locked up.
Shop, storage and home moves
Getting a bike to a shop, into storage or back home. Have both addresses ready when you call.
What to tell us
The make, model and rough weight, whether the keys are with it, and anything custom to be careful around, like bags, fairings or pipes.
Call (209) 612-9092or text us about a bike

Winching and recovery

Recovery is for a vehicle that has left the pavement or can't drive out on its own. A winch pulls it back to where it can be loaded or driven. The photo here is a real Superior1 recovery: a pickup nose-down in a flooded roadside ditch.

Winch-outs
For a vehicle stuck in a ditch, in mud or on a soft shoulder. Tell us what it's stuck in and how deep the wheels are.
Off-road recoveries
For a vehicle down an embankment or out in a field. Tell us how far it is from the road and whether a truck can get close.
Towed after the pull
If it can't be driven once it's out, it can go on the flatbed. Have a drop-off address ready in case.
Send a photo first
If you can do it safely, text a picture that shows the whole vehicle and the ground around it. If anyone is hurt or the vehicle is in a traffic lane, call 911 first.
Text a photo and locationor call (209) 612-9092

24-hour roadside assistance

If it can be fixed where you're parked, you may not need a tow. Roadside service covers cars and trucks, and some services cover semis, bobtails and box trucks too.

Jump starts and battery service
For a vehicle that clicks, cranks slowly or is completely dead. If it dies again after a jump, the battery or charging system may need attention.
Lockouts
Keys on the seat, in the trunk or behind a locked door. Have the year, make and model ready, and tell us whether the vehicle is running.
Flat tires and spare changes
We swap the flat for your spare so you can get moving. Check that the spare holds air, and have the key if your wheels use locking lug nuts.
Fuel delivery
Ran out of gas? We bring some to you so you can reach a station. Say exactly where you stopped and what kind of fuel the vehicle takes.
Semis, bobtails and box trucks
Jump starts and lockouts are offered for semis, bobtails and box trucks. Tell us which one it is and where it's parked.
While you wait
Pull as far off the road as you safely can and turn on your hazard lights. If you feel unsafe, call 911.
Call (209) 612-9092or text us where you are

Equipment transportation and hauling

For planned moves, when nothing is broken and something heavy needs to be somewhere else. Call ahead with the size, the weight and both addresses.

Equipment transportation
Machines moved between jobs, yards and shops, like the skid steer in this photo. Have the make, model and weight, and tell us if it drives.
Local hauling
Moves around Lathrop and the 209. Let us know about gates, tight driveways or soft ground at either end.
Long distance hauling
For longer moves, send the pickup city, the drop-off city and the day you need it there, and ask for a quote.
Container transportation
Share the container's length, whether it's empty, and how much room there is to load it and set it down.

Getting a tow, step by step

  1. Call or text (209) 612-9092

Common questions

Are you really open 24 hours?

Yes. Superior1 is open 24 hours a day, Monday through Sunday, for towing and roadside assistance. Call or text (209) 612-9092.

Can I text instead of calling?

Yes. The same number takes calls and texts. For anything urgent, calling is the faster way to explain what's going on.

What should I have ready when I call?

Your exact location, the year, make and model, what happened, whether the vehicle rolls and steers, and where you want it taken. A photo helps with recoveries and anything oversized.

How much does a tow cost?

It depends on the vehicle, the distance and how hard it is to reach. Call or text the details and ask for a quote.

What kinds of payment do you take?

Apple Pay, Zelle, cash and all major credit cards.

Can you take a lowered car or a lifted truck?

Yes, both are on our service list. Tell us about the ride height, tire size and any custom parts so we know before we load.

Do you do long distance tows?

Long distance hauling is on our service list. Send the pickup city, the drop-off city and your timing, and ask for a quote.

Do you help semis and box trucks?

Yes, with jump starts and lockouts for semis, bobtails and box trucks. If one needs to be towed, call and we'll tell you if it's something we can do.

Where should I wait?

Somewhere safe and away from traffic, with your hazard lights on. If you feel unsafe or someone is hurt, call 911 before you call us.
